ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows a complementary push-pull output circuit, with the right side connected to the load resistor R_L through a coupling capacitor; the upper end of the load R_L is marked with the positive terminal of the output voltage u_o, and the lower end is grounded and marked with the negative terminal, so u_o is the sinusoidal output voltage applied across R_L. The problem gives V_CC=30 V, R_L=6 Ω, and states that after adjustment the output has no distortion; at this time the maximum output voltage is 12 V. Then reason: According to the meaning of the problem and the labeling in the figure, the maximum output voltage 12 V is taken as the peak value U_m of the undistorted sinusoidal output voltage. The effective value of the sinusoidal voltage is U_rms=U_m/√2=12/√2 V. The output average power is P_o=U_rms^2/R_L=(12/√2)^2/6=12^2/(2×6)=144/12=12 W.

method.method_draft: From the diagram, identify u_o as the sinusoidal voltage across R_L. From the text take R_L=6 ohm and maximum output voltage U_m=12 V. Treat 12 V as the peak value of the undistorted sine wave, convert to rms: U_rms=12/sqrt(2) V, then compute P_o=U_rms^2/R_L=12^2/(2*6)=12 W.
